kata.name: Flyweight sharing law F-Handle: the client-handle co-reference equation catches the rerouted handle (one executed equation violation; the conventional handle test catches it too — parity)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md (Flyweight row, re-opened by naming the law first); fixtures/katas/flyweight/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.8
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the sharing law's handle projection is expressible as the path equation key x factory = flyweight, comparing target row ids rather than values; it is expected to fire on the client whose handle names a different row, and the conventional handle assertion names the same element, so unique is empty (parity)

expected.detail: client 1 holds row 0 while factory(key(client 1)) is row 1, and the two rows carry distinct intrinsic states; equation 0 fires on row 1 with lhs row 1 and rhs row 0 — a co-reference mismatch, not a value difference. Injectivity holds and both rows are factory images, so only the handle equation sees the fault

commands: python3 prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 2 clean + 4 fault fixtures match the pre-registered detections
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/flyweight/flyweight-fault-rerouted-handle.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert, executed before the probe arm: the handle-identity assertion compares the client's handle row to the factory's row for its key and names the same element

baseline.artifact: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py sha256:c5c9c28bc4e1bb75a7b2fb64bf41a66d908cd3fee468f7fd00150c26cdbd6d30 (scripted conventional Flyweight test: handle identity, interning pairs, pool closure)

expressibility_gap.invariant: runtime object identity, aliasing, lifetime, and mutation
expressibility_gap.why: F-Handle is a declared-row co-reference: both paths resolve to the same dense row id. The kernel has no notion of runtime object identity, reference counting, GC lifetime, or mutation after the document is written, and no such claim is made

discrepancies: `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 3` on the clean base still raises flyweight x intrinsic vs key x factory x intrinsic as a hypothesized parallel path: the kernel asks the composite consequence of the accepted handle equation instead of deriving it. Recorded as an observation and never counted as a detection
the equation compares dense row ids, so its success is co-reference in the model; the model's rows are the identity notion, not runtime objects
procedure: 1. The law was named before the fixtures (README 'Law named first'): F-Intern (declarative key on the intrinsic tuple), F-Handle (path equation key x factory = flyweight), plus the two laws named as unexpressible (F-Closure, F-Capacity). The fault set and its expectations were pinned in fixtures/katas/flyweight/faults.json.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/flyweight_baseline.py, sha256 pinned in comparison.baseline) was executed first: the complete conventional Flyweight contract (handle identity per client, interning pairs over declared rows, pool closure), never calling catherine.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, findings recorded verbatim; no kernel change and no new CLI.

4. Witnesses were mapped to the pre-registered element vocabulary: an equation witness {equation, row} to flyweight:handle-identity@Client#<row>; a key witness {key, rows:[lo,hi]} to flyweight:interning-pair@Flyweight#<lo>/Flyweight#<hi>; baseline-only pool-closure elements carry no probe counterpart. unique = probe elements minus baseline elements.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived. Expressibility is recorded separately in expressibility_gap and never inflates the verdict.
